## Project Overview: LEX PRO (LexPro)

A **law-firm office management system** (نظام إدارة مكاتب المحاماة). It is a **npm workspaces monorepo** packaged as an **Electron desktop app** (Windows NSIS installer) with an Express/MongoDB backend. The root `package.json` declares 4 workspaces: `packages/shared`, `packages/server`, `packages/renderer`, `packages/main`.

Root `package.json` key scripts: `dev` (concurrently runs server+renderer+main), `build` (builds renderer→server→main), `package` (`build` + `electron-builder --config electron-builder.json`). Root devDeps: vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, concurrently, cross-env, electron-builder, sqlite3, wait-on. Root dep: electron.

---

### 1. ALL files in `packages/server/src/` (10 source files)
- `packages/server/src/index.ts` — entry point
- `packages/server/src/config/database.ts` — Mongo connection + Mega init
- `packages/server/src/models/index.ts` — all Mongoose models (464 lines)
- `packages/server/src/routes/index.ts` — all API routes (1274 lines)
- `packages/server/src/middleware/auth.ts` — JWT auth + RBAC
- `packages/server/src/middleware/error.ts` — error/404 handlers
- `packages/server/src/middleware/upload.ts` — multer memory storage (100MB limit)
- `packages/server/src/middleware/activityLogger.ts` — audit logging via Socket.io
- `packages/server/src/services/mega.ts` — Mega cloud file storage (ACTIVE)
- `packages/server/src/services/gridfs.ts` — GridFS file storage (LEGACY/UNUSED — see notes)

A compiled `packages/server/dist/` already exists (mirrors src). Server `tsconfig.json`: target ES2022, commonjs, outDir `dist`, rootDir `src`, path alias `"@lexpro/shared": ["../shared/src"]`, references `../shared`.

### 2. `packages/server/package.json`
- Name `@lexpro/server`, main `dist/index.js`. Scripts: `dev` (tsx watch), `build` (tsc), `start` (node dist/index.js).

## Project Overview: LEX PRO (LexPro)

A **law-firm office management system** (نظام إدارة مكاتب المحاماة). It is a **npm workspaces monorepo** packaged as an **Electron desktop app** (Windows NSIS installer) with an Express/MongoDB backend. The root `package.json` declares 4 workspaces: `packages/shared`, `packages/server`, `packages/renderer`, `packages/main`.

Root `package.json` key scripts: `dev` (concurrently runs server+renderer+main), `build` (builds renderer→server→main), `package` (`build` + `electron-builder --config electron-builder.json`). Root devDeps: vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, concurrently, cross-env, electron-builder, sqlite3, wait-on. Root dep: electron.

---

### 1. ALL files in `packages/server/src/` (10 source files)
- `packages/server/src/index.ts` — entry point
- `packages/server/src/config/database.ts` — Mongo connection + Mega init
- `packages/server/src/models/index.ts` — all Mongoose models (464 lines)
- `packages/server/src/routes/index.ts` — all API routes (1274 lines)
- `packages/server/src/middleware/auth.ts` — JWT auth + RBAC
- `packages/server/src/middleware/error.ts` — error/404 handlers
- `packages/server/src/middleware/upload.ts` — multer memory storage (100MB limit)
- `packages/server/src/middleware/activityLogger.ts` — audit logging via Socket.io
- `packages/server/src/services/mega.ts` — Mega cloud file storage (ACTIVE)
- `packages/server/src/services/gridfs.ts` — GridFS file storage (LEGACY/UNUSED — see notes)

A compiled `packages/server/dist/` already exists (mirrors src). Server `tsconfig.json`: target ES2022, commonjs, outDir `dist`, rootDir `src`, path alias `"@lexpro/shared": ["../shared/src"]`, references `../shared`.

### 2. `packages/server/package.json`
- Name `@lexpro/server`, main `dist/index.js`. Scripts: `dev` (tsx watch), `build` (tsc), `start` (node dist/index.js).
- **Dependencies**: bcryptjs, cors, dotenv, express, gridfs-stream, jsonwebtoken, megajs, mongoose, multer, pdfkit, socket.io.
- **devDependencies**: @types/* for bcryptjs, cors, express, jsonwebtoken, multer, pdfkit, tsx, typescript.

### 3. Environment files
- `packages/server/.env` **EXISTS** on disk and contains (plaintext credentials — security concern):
  ```
  MEGA_EMAIL=amrmansour8374@gmail.com
  MEGA_PASSWORD=amrAMR123
  ```
- **No `.env.example`** anywhere. No root `.env`. `.gitignore` excludes `.env` and `.env.local`, so this file should NOT be committed (verify with `git check-ignore`).
- The server reads `.env` from `path.join(__dirname, '..', '.env')` (i.e. `packages/server/.env`) in `index.ts`, and `mega.ts` re-loads it from `packages/server/.env` too.

### 4. `packages/shared/` and how the server uses it
- Contents: `package.json` (name `@lexpro/shared`, main/types point to `src/index.ts`), `tsconfig.json`, and `src/index.ts` plus pre-built `index.js/.d.ts/.map` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`.
- `src/index.ts` is a **pure TypeScript type-definitions file** (~300 lines) exporting interfaces: ICustomer, ICourt, ICaseType, ICase, ICaseSession, ICaseDocument, ISessionDocument, ICaseAnnouncement, IAnnouncementDocument, ICustomerDocument, IDocumentTemplate, IFeeAgreement, IFeePayment, IFeeHistory, IExpense, IExpenseDocument, ILawyerProfile, ISystemInfo, IApiResponse, IDashboardStats, ICustomerDossier, ICourtDossier, INotificationItem, IBackupSettings, ITask.
- **CRITICAL deployment finding**: `@lexpro/shared` is referenced ONLY as a tsconfig path alias in `packages/server/tsconfig.json`. A grep for `@lexpro/shared` across `packages/server` found **zero imports in any `.ts` source file** — the server does NOT actually import shared types at runtime. The shared package is effectively unused by the server today; it's a build-time-only path mapping (and the server compiles fine without consuming it).

### 5. Deployment configs — NONE
- No `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml/yaml`, `Procfile`, `.dockerignore`, or any `*.dockerfile` found anywhere in the project.
- The only "packaging" config is `electron-builder.json` (appId `com.lexpro.app`, productName "LEX PRO", output `dist-electron`, Windows NSIS target, icon `build/icon.ico`). It bundles `packages/{main,renderer,server}/dist/**` + `node_modules/**`. This builds a **desktop installer**, not a server deployment artifact.

### 6. `.gitignore` (root)
```
node_modules/
dist/
build/
*.log
.DS_Store
.env
.env.local
bordup.db
```
Note: `dist/` is ignored, yet `packages/server/dist/` and `packages/shared/src/*.js` exist on disk (build artifacts). `bordup.db` suggests a legacy SQLite DB.

### 7. Server entry point `packages/server/src/index.ts`
- Loads dotenv from `packages/server/.env`; creates Express app; `PORT = process.env.PORT || 3001`.
- Middleware: `cors()` (open, origin '*'), `express.json({limit:'100mb'})`, urlencoded 100mb.
- Mounts routes at `/api`. Error/404 handlers.
- Creates HTTP server + Socket.io (cors origin '*'). Tracks online users in a `Map<userId, socketId>`; exports `io`, `isUserOnline`, `getOnlineUserIds`.
- `seedAdmin()`: creates default admin `admin / admin123` (bcrypt hash) if none exists — **hardcoded default credentials, security concern**.
- `cleanupOldActivityLogs()`: deletes ActivityLogs older than 48h, runs hourly via setInterval.
- `start()`: connectDatabase → seedAdmin → cleanup → listen on PORT.

### 8. Server-specific build scripts/configs
- Server build = plain `tsc` (no bundler). `tsconfig.json` outputs CommonJS to `dist/` with declarations+sourcemaps.
- `scripts/start-main.cmd` exists (Windows batch launcher for the Electron main process; referenced by root `dev:main` as `wait-on http://localhost:5173 && scripts\start-main.cmd`). Its exact content couldn't be re-fetched (tool cache quirk) but it's a dev-only launcher.
- `postcss.config.js` (tailwindcss + autoprefixer) — renderer-side, not server.

### 9. Root `read-db.js` / `read-db-data.js`
Both are **standalone SQLite inspection scripts** for a **legacy "BordUp" desktop app**, NOT part of the current server. They open `C:\Users\Mahmoud\AppData\Roaming\BordUp\lawfirm.db` via `sqlite3`:
- `read-db.js`: lists all tables, their columns, and 3 sample rows each.
- `read-db-data.js`: dumps all rows from a hardcoded list of tables (Courts, CaseTypes, AnnouncementTypes, Customers, Cases, CaseSessions, CaseAnnouncements, CaseDocuments, SessionDocuments, AnnouncementDocuments, CustomerDocuments, DocumentTemplates, FeeAgreements, FeePayments, FeeHistories, Expenses, ExpenseDocuments, LawyerProfiles, SystemInfos).
These appear to be one-off migration/data-inspection helpers (the table names mirror the current Mongoose models, suggesting a past SQLite→MongoDB migration). `sqlite3` is a root devDependency.

### 10. Root `tsconfig.json` and other configs
- Root `tsconfig.json`: target ES2022, module ESNext, moduleResolution "bundler", strict, declaration+sourceMap. (No `include`/`references` — base config for the renderer/main packages.)
- `packages/shared/tsconfig.json`: same base + `include: ["src/**/*"]`.
- `packages/server/tsconfig.json`: CommonJS, outDir dist, rootDir src, path alias + project reference to shared (detailed above).
- `electron-builder.json`, `postcss.config.js` covered above.
- `build/` directory contains only `icon.ico` and `icon.png` (app icons).

**Server architecture (from models + routes):**
- MongoDB models (`models/index.ts`): LawyerProfile, Court, CaseType, AnnouncementType, Customer, Case, CaseSession, CaseDocument, SessionDocument, CaseAnnouncement, AnnouncementDocument, CustomerDocument, DocumentTemplate, FeeAgreement, FeePayment, FeeHistory, Expense, ExpenseDocument, SystemInfo, Task, User (with role enum admin/lawyer/secretary + per-module permissions), ActivityLog, Message (chat), FileReference (links a short id to a Mega URL). `MODULE_NAMES` exported.

functionDeclarations.name: search_file_content
functionDeclarations.description: Searches for a regular expression pattern within the content of files in a specified directory, a specific file, or the current working directory. The search backend is ripgrep, so regex patterns use ripgrep/Rust regex syntax, not JavaScript RegExp syntax. If you need to search literal text that contains regex metacharacters (for example $, {, [, (, or \), set fixed_strings: true or -F: true instead of escaping by hand. Can filter files by a glob pattern when searching directories. By default, returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers; set output_mode to "files_with_matches" for just file paths or "count" for per-file match totals. Each matched line is truncated at 500 characters with a "[line truncated from N chars]" suffix to keep minified or base64 content from blowing up context.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for within file contents. This is interpreted by ripgrep/Rust regex, not JavaScript RegExp; avoid JS-only features such as lookbehind and backreferences. Regex syntax errors are returned by ripgrep. For literal text, especially strings containing regex metacharacters like $, {, [, (, or \, prefer fixed_strings: true or -F: true. When passing JSON args, escape only for JSON once: to match literal ${, use pattern "\\$\\{" (the regex engine sees \$\{), not "\\\\$\\\\{".

path.description: Optional: A path relative to the workspace root, or an absolute path to a directory or file to search within. If a file path is provided, searches only within that file. If a directory path is provided, searches all files in that directory. If omitted, searches the current working directory.

glob.description: Optional: A glob pattern to filter which files are searched (e.g., '*.js', '*.{ts,tsx}', 'src/**'). Single string only — combine multiple patterns via whitespace/comma separation (e.g. '*.js *.ts', '*.js,*.ts') or brace expansion ('*.{ts,tsx}'). Only applicable when searching directories, ignored for file searches. If omitted, searches all files (respecting potential global ignores).

output_mode.description: Optional: Output format. 'content' (default) returns matching lines with line numbers and optional context; 'files_with_matches' returns only the list of matching file paths; 'count' returns per-file match counts.

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of matches to return to prevent context overflow (default: 250, max: 1000). Values above 1000 are clamped automatically. Use lower values for broad searches, higher for specific searches. Pass 0 for unlimited.

head_limit.description: Optional: Claude Code aligned alias for 'maxResults'. When both are provided, head_limit wins. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Optional: Number of matches to skip before returning results. Use this to continue after a truncated result's next offset.

-A.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -A.

-B.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -B.

-C.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -C.

context.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for -C.

-n.description: Optional: Whether to include line numbers in 'content' output. Defaults to true; set to false to omit them.

-i.description: Optional: Case-insensitive matching. Defaults to false (case-sensitive), matching ripgrep behavior.

fixed_strings.description: Optional: Treat the pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression. Alias for -F.

-F.description: Optional: Treat the pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression. Alias for fixed_strings.

type.description: Optional: ripgrep file type filter (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. Accepts any alias from `rg --type-list`; the value is forwarded verbatim to ripgrep.

multiline.description: Optional: Enable multiline matching where patterns may span newlines (passes -U and --multiline-dotall to ripgrep). Only meaningful for 'content' output_mode. ^/$ anchors keep line boundaries behavior for portability across search backends.

include_hidden.description: Optional: Whether to descend into dot-prefixed directories (e.g. '.git/', '.codely-cli/') and match dot-prefixed files. Defaults to false to mirror ripgrep's default hidden-skip behaviour. Set to true to scan hidden paths explicitly (passes --hidden to ripgrep).
